title: Warn loudly on person-file key changes not signed by an old key
description: Confirmed 2026-10-22 against git-vouch:886-889: check validates only the current snapshot. Anyone whose merge lands (incl. the registry maintainer) can replace people/<handle>.json with new keys self-signed by those new keys; the handle-only tier record and endorsements carry over. Contradicts DESIGN.md claims that the merger cannot forge a change and that endorsements carry over because rotation was signed by the old key. Fix needs a decision from Mark: (a) check walks git history of people/ and requires each new version to be signed by a key current in the previous version (or anchor-signed recovery); (b) tier records bind subjectKey like endorsements do, with rotation following a signed chain; (c) both.
acceptance_criteria: Fixture registry history with (1) a rotation signed by the old key: no warning; (2) a replacement signed only by new keys: prominent warning naming handle/commit/old+new did:keys, check still exits 0 if nothing else is wrong. Real ssh-keygen signatures.
notes:
DECIDED (Mark, 2026-10-22): registry review is the gate; accepted risk like anchors.json. check never fails on this, but walks git history of people/ and prints a prominent WARNING for every version whose .sig has no valid signature from a key current in the previous version (lost key or swap), naming handle, commit, old and new did:keys. Lost-key recovery = a reviewed merge; tier carries over. DESIGN.md claims ('merger cannot forge', 'endorsements carry over because rotation was signed by the old key') must be reworded to match.
DECIDED D11 (Mark, 2026-10-22): a person file change needs a signature from ANY ONE key current in the previous version (not every current key), so backup tokens stay in the drawer. Replaces verify_person's 'one signature per current key' rule (git-vouch:708-742). First version of a person file: signed by at least one of its own keys.
